summary: Poland’s excerpts emphasize an EU-wide ecosystem framework, with no quantified Poland-specific restoration-area target. For conservation and mixed land-use commitments, they call for halting and reversing deforestation and forest degradation by 2030 and restoration measures in at least 20% of EU land areas and 20% of sea areas by 2030, with all ecosystems needing restoration by 2050. The LULUCF framework sets 310 Mt CO2-eq of net removals by 2030 (carbon-sinks notation: −310 Mt CO2-eq), with an additional 42 Mt CO2-eq versus the 2016–2018 average; Poland’s listed national target is −3,278 Kt CO2eq. Agricultural finance provisions assign 40% of the EU CAP allocation in 2023–2027 to climate objectives, 25% of direct-payment funds to eco-schemes, and 35% of Pillar II funds to environment and climate. Poland’s current land cover is 58.5% agricultural, 32.4% forest, and 5.2% grassland, but no Polish hectare target permits a direct land-cover comparison.
